title: Flowise Alternatives in 2026: Top Picks Compared
summary: Flowise alternatives address different needs: chatbot replacement, agents with approvals, or enterprise control. Select based on your main constraint.
body_markdown:
## 4. Activepieces as a Flowise alternative


If your agent has to do something in a business app and wait for a person to approve it, Activepieces fits. Its core is MIT-licensed, so you can run it yourself, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


That's the fix for the problem the last section described: approval steps you wire up by hand, in a tool built for exactly that wiring.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) has an MIT-licensed core, so you can self-host it on your own infrastructure and keep workflow data inside your network. The enterprise directories sit under a separate commercial licence.


There's also a hosted cloud version if you'd rather not run it, and unlimited flows come with every plan, including the free one.


If you self-host, you carry the upgrades, the backups and the uptime, which is the trade you already made if you ran Flowise yourself.


I won't quote tier prices here; check the pricing page before you budget, and look at how cost scales with runs, since an hourly trigger multiplies quickly.


Think of the agent as a step inside an automation, not a separate chat product.


Its AI step works across the platform's[integrations, which Activepieces calls pieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) , 741 of them counted from the open source monorepo, so the same flow can read a spreadsheet row, ask a model what to do, and write the result to another app.


Look at the builder to see how that's put together. The canvas holds a three-step flow: an Every Hour trigger, an Ask ChatGPT action, and an End node.


The open Select Step panel has a search box (here, "sheet") and returns Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel 365, AITable and Kimai.


The point is that adding a model call and adding an app action use the same picker, so you never leave the canvas to give the agent somewhere to act.


In the same canvas you get approval steps. You place a human check before the step that writes, and the flow pauses there. You build it, so the gate sits only where you put it.


It's not a RAG-first canvas. If you left Flowise because you wanted better control over chunking, retrievers and vector stores, Activepieces will feel thin there.


It's built around triggers and actions across those 741 integrations, and retrieval is something you assemble rather than the thing the product is organized around.


It suits teams whose agent's job ends in an action, such as updating a record, sending a message or filing a row, and who want a person to sign off first. If that's you, you can[try it free](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Fflowise-alternatives-in-2026-top-picks-compared) .


It suits you less if retrieval quality is the whole job.


Activepieces is the better fit for teams that need an agent to act in business apps with human approval, and that want governance in a single product rather than assembled from parts.


RBAC, SSO, SCIM, audit logs, log and event streaming, and environments with git sync all ship together, whether you self-host or use the cloud, with no cut-down version either way.


If your deciding criterion is having approvals and governance under one roof, with an MIT-licensed core you can run inside your own network, Activepieces is the better choice. Note that the enterprise directories sit under a separate commercial licence.
